classification.difficultyReason: Apply graphical symmetry in parts (a) and (b), then recognise in part (c) that the supplied nonzero value at the origin prevents any odd completion, requiring a connection between graphical symmetry and f(0)=0.

content.prompt: Complete the graphs below so that they represent even and odd functions. Draw your graphs on separate axes.

spec.description: Unscaled coordinate sketch. The supplied branch starts at the origin and rises to the right with increasing steepness. No formula or numerical scale is asserted.
spec.mathematics: Given branch for x at least zero; complete by reflection or origin symmetry.

answer.short: Even: reflect the given branch in the $y$-axis. Odd: rotate the given branch through $180^\circ$ about the origin.
answer.worked:
For an even function, $f(-x)=f(x)$, so add the reflection of the given branch in the $y$-axis.

For an odd function, $f(-x)=-f(x)$, so add the image of the given branch under a $180^\circ$ rotation about the origin. Draw the completions on separate axes.

spec.description: Complete even sketch on its own axes; the added branch is the exact reflection of the schematic supplied branch.
Complete odd sketch on separate axes.
spec.mathematics: The added branch is the image under (x,y) mapped to (-x,-y).

spec.description: Unscaled first-quadrant branch beginning at the origin, rising to one rounded maximum and then falling while remaining above the x-axis. Schematic Bézier reconstruction; no formula, maximum coordinates or asymptote is asserted.
spec.mathematics: A supplied single-valued branch for positive inputs, including the origin.

answer.short: Even: reflect the given branch in the $y$-axis. Odd: rotate the given branch through $180^\circ$ about the origin.
answer.worked:
For the even completion, reflect each point $(x,y)$ to $(-x,y)$.

For the odd completion, rotate each point $(x,y)$ to $(-x,-y)$. The reflected hump is above the negative $x$-axis in the even sketch and below it in the odd sketch.

spec.description: Complete even sketch on its own axes, retaining the supplied hump and adding its y-axis reflection.
Complete odd sketch on separate axes, with the added trough below the negative x-axis.

Left-hand branch crossing the x-axis at -1 and reaching the y-axis at -1 without an open endpoint marker. The source supplies no equation, so the curve is reconstructed schematically through its stated intercepts.
spec.mathematics: The supplied value at zero is -1; this prevents an odd extension preserving the entire branch.

answer.short: Even: reflect the given branch in the $y$-axis. An odd completion is impossible while retaining the supplied point $(0,-1)$.
answer.worked:
Reflecting the given branch in the $y$-axis gives an even function with intercepts $(-1,0)$ and $(1,0)$ and value $f(0)=-1$.

For an odd function,
$$\begin{align*}f(0)&=-f(0)\\2f(0)&=0\\f(0)&=0.\end{align*}$$
The supplied graph has $f(0)=-1$, so no odd function can preserve it. Rotating the branch would also place a point at $(0,1)$, giving two outputs at zero.

spec.description: Valid even completion. No purported odd solution is drawn because the given value at zero makes one impossible.
